title: Coroner's jury suggests changes after teen's death
subtitle: Jury says Ontario should consider limiting when police can shoot at cars
article: Duane Christian, 15, died June 20, 2006, after a confrontation with two police officers near an apartment complex in the area of Scarborough Golf Club Road and Lawrence Avenue East.
Christian was not armed but he was driving a stolen van at the time. The constable who shot Christian said he had to shoot to prevent his partner from being deliberately run down.
In August 2006, the province's Special Investigations Unit concluded that the officer's actions were legally justified because he feared his partner would be struck and killed by the van.

In 2008, the Toronto Police Service amended its use-of-force guidelines to prohibit police from firing their weapons at a driver or passenger of the vehicle unless there's a threat of serious injury or death from something other than the vehicle.
On Thursday, the coroner's jury recommended that Ontario "study the possibility of enacting" the revised Toronto policy across the province.
Peter Thorning, lawyer for the two officers involved, said he disagrees with the recommendation because it could limit an officer's ability to protect themselves or members of the public.
"I've always maintained that this policy is a silly policy," Thorning said. "There are many reports of vehicles being used as weapons in homicides."
But Peter Rosenthal, the lawyer for Christian's family, said the recommendation should prompt police officials to make sure officers understand the policies guiding use of force.

The five-member jury also recommended that Toronto police officers be given extra training to explain the reasons behind the policy. The jury also suggested that the Toronto Police Service introduce an outreach program that works with youth in the city's priority neighbourhoods.
